# SPACE FRONTIER — Build a Future Beyond Earth

A 3D space-exploration and Mars-outpost simulator for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026,
challenge **“Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer”**.

Fly a spacecraft around Mars, land, drive a rover, and run a research base where power, air, water,
food and radiation all depend on each other.

## Run it

Requires Node.js 20 or newer.

```bash
npm install
```

```bash
npm run dev
```

Then open http://localhost:5173.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Start the game locally |
| `npm test` | Run the automated test suite (80 tests currently) |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check |
| `npm run build` | Production build into `dist/` (a static site, no server needed) |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally at http://localhost:4173 |
| `npm run simulate -- 1000` | Balance tester for the base engine (classic 15-sol mode) |
| `node scripts/fetch-nasa.mjs` | Re-download the NASA data snapshots |
details:
# SPACE FRONTIER — Build a Future Beyond Earth

A 3D space-exploration and Mars-outpost simulator for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026,

challenge **“Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer”**.

Fly a spacecraft around Mars, land, drive a rover, and run a research base where power, air, water,

food and radiation all depend on each other.

## Run it

Requires Node.js 20 or newer.

```bash

npm install

```

```bash

npm run dev

```

Then open http://localhost:5173.

| Command | What it does |

|---|---|

| `npm run dev` | Start the game locally |

| `npm test` | Run the automated test suite (80 tests currently) |

| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check |

| `npm run build` | Production build into `dist/` (a static site, no server needed) |

| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally at http://localhost:4173 |

| `npm run simulate -- 1000` | Balance tester for the base engine (classic 15-sol mode) |

| `node scripts/fetch-nasa.mjs` | Re-download the NASA data snapshots |

## Three-minute demo path

1. Select **New expedition**, then **Begin** to close the briefing.

2. In orbit, select **To land, first fly to low Mars orbit**. Wait for the low-orbit message, then choose **Land → Rover**.

3. In the rover navigator, choose a nearby unfinished site and **Drive there**. When the rover arrives, press **E** to collect a sample or complete the site job; show the result card.

4. Switch **You are here → Base** and click the **Command Center** building. Review the crew jobs and power plan.

5. Select **End the sol…**. Review the forecast's made, used, after, and storage-limit values, then choose **End the sol ▶** to advance one simulated day and open the actual Sol Report.

6. Open **☰ Menu → Mission debrief** to show this run's ledger totals, event decisions, and state-based recommendation. It updates from the simulation's sol reports; the final expedition results still appear when the mission ends.

If time is short, skip the rover site action and land directly at **Base**. The forecast and report still provide a complete, repeatable resource-management demo.

## How to play

- **Spacecraft:** `W`/`S` speed, `A`/`D` turn, `R`/`F` nose up/down, `Space` brake, `E` use. Or pick a target and press **Autopilot**.

- **Rover:** `W`/`S` drive, `A`/`D` steer, `E` start the job at a site. Or pick a site and press **Auto-drive**.

- **Astronaut EVA:** stop the rover and choose **Get out and walk (EVA)** in the rover navigator. Walk with `W`/`S` and `A`/`D`; use `E` near a site or building. Press `X` or **Get back in the rover** to return. The HUD shows the safety distance; EVA work adds simulated radiation dose.

- **Camera:** drag to look around, scroll to zoom.

- **Moving around:** the “You are here” bar switches between Orbit, Rover, Base and Greenhouse. To land, fly into low Mars orbit first.

- **Base:** click a building. Time only moves when you press **End the sol**; a forecast is shown first.

- **Radiation shield:** click the Crew Habitat and send astronauts to pile soil over it.

- Touch devices get on-screen controls.

## What is in the game

| Area | What you do |

|---|---|

| Space | Fly a third-person spacecraft between Mars, the orbital station, Phobos, Deimos and a deployment point. Scan, dock, deploy. |

| Mars surface | Drive a rover to ten sites: rock samples, radiation sensors, EVAs (weather mast, solar array, seismometer), a site survey. |

| Research base | A 3D base drawn from the live simulation: habitat, command center, greenhouse, lab, recycler, oxygen maker, solar arrays, batteries, comms, storage tanks. |

| Greenhouse | Walk-in hydroponics: set light, nutrients, temperature and water flow, and watch the plants respond sol by sol. |

| Lab | Growth-chamber comparison experiments and a microbe bioreactor. |

| Missions | Seven connected missions with objectives, measurable results and a short explanation. |

| Academy | Six lessons (orbits, sunlight, hydroponics, water chemistry, Mars, radiation). Each has an experiment and a quiz, and unlocks something in the game. |

| Science Data | Viewer for every real dataset used, with sources. |

## NASA data used

| Source | How it was obtained | Used for |

|---|---|---|

| **NASA DONKI** solar flare (FLR) and solar energetic particle (SEP) records, last 12 months | Downloaded by `scripts/fetch-nasa.mjs` on 2026-11-14 from `https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI-API/get/` | Solar-storm events at the base (real date and flare class), the space-weather monitor, the data viewer |

| **NASA POWER** climatology, Kennedy Space Center | Downloaded by the same script on 2026-11-14 | Earth sunlight above the air and at the ground, in the sunlight lesson and data viewer |

| **NASA NSSDCA Mars Fact Sheet** | Read on 2026-11-14, values typed into `src/sim/science.ts` | Orbits of Phobos and Deimos (distance and period to scale), gravity, sunlight, atmosphere |

| Hassler et al. 2014 (Curiosity RAD), NASA Veggie, ISS water recovery, InSight | Cited from published work, not re-downloaded | Reference values and real-world context in lessons and result cards |

Honesty rules the game follows:

- Snapshots are labelled **ARCHIVED** with their retrieval date. Nothing is presented as live.

(DONKI sends no CORS header, so a browser cannot call it directly.)

- Every number on a result card is tagged **NASA DATA**, **CALCULATED** or **SIMULATED**.

- The Mars terrain, the look of the planet, samples, sensor readings at game sites, the hydroponics

and microbe models, and all base numbers are **simulations**. Their shapes follow real science,

but they are simplified and time-compressed.

- A real flare is not claimed to have hit Mars. The event card says we imagine it did.

## Architecture in one paragraph

Simulation is separate from rendering. `src/engine/` is the original tested base engine (pure, seeded,

one sol per tick). `src/sim/` holds the newer pure models: flight, rover, terrain, hydroponics,

biology, orbital physics, missions, and the per-sol integration that connects the greenhouse and lab

to the engine. `src/store/` wraps them in two Zustand stores. `src/three/` renders the three

environments with React Three Fiber using only procedural geometry and textures (no asset files).

`src/ui/` is the HUD, panels and menus drawn over the 3D view. See `docs/ARCHITECTURE_3D.md`.

## Known limits

- NASA DONKI and POWER data are archived snapshots, not live feeds. The Mars terrain, EVA readings, and resource economy are simplified simulations, not certified astronaut training.

- The 3D scenes require browser WebGL support. The production JavaScript bundle is about 1.3 MB minified; Vite reports a chunk-size advisory.

- See “What is not done” in `docs/ARCHITECTURE_3D.md` for the full list.
